The owner now authorizes a planning-only task: “Confer with GPT and define the next module in the approved dependency order, with concrete scope and acceptance criteria. Once done, push everything to Github. Report to GPT confirmation info.”

Current clean Engine HEAD and remote acceptance commit is e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d. Your actual Consecration verdict a34a0fba-bc6a-51c7-96d3-3a142e4028a7 and Codex agreement are retained there. Runtime remains3c5135ae; full1587 reconciliation/five428-command paths and all prior exact acceptances stand. The broader goal remains paused; this request authorizes defining and publishing the successor contract, not implementation or Unity integration.

Please inspect the current implementation map/status, pre-Unity completion contract, accepted prerequisite/operational sequence and relevant retained source contracts. Recommend exactly ONE next implementation module in the approved dependency order. Give:
1. Module identity, dependency rationale and exact prerequisite acceptance references; distinguish formal graph edges from scoped operational prerequisites. Do not assume Consecration completion authorizes the entire class/resurrection chain.
2. Concrete source-bound in-scope behavior and required owning/public APIs, shared-state/clock/RNG/inventory/work/conditions/persistence integration.
3. Explicit exclusions, unresolved source/API decisions and stop conditions—no invented mechanics, silent scope reductions or new production authority.
4. Testable acceptance criteria including genuine connected gameplay, negative/boundary/authority/privacy cases, supported old saves, deterministic replay, source/build/test evidence, and actual final module review.
5. Whether any prerequisite contract or capability must close before implementation can start; do not label a proposal as already accepted.

Please compare the known CG-CONTEXT-01 integration gap, the held Saint/resurrection prerequisites, and other mapped prerequisites as appropriate; choose based on the approved plan rather than automatically picking a convenient adjacent feature. Reuse existing accepted work. Do NOT edit code, run gameplay/tests, start a module, change the graph or reopen accepted TAC-10/Consecration allocations. I will inspect the exact source/current APIs locally, prepare the concrete contract and map update, return it for your actual planning review, then push agreed documentation and report the verified GitHub commit. Repo: https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/tree/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity

**Recommend exactly one successor: a bounded TAC-01 ordinary-world magical-activity calendar integration module, closing `CG-CONTEXT-01` for the existing admitted post-encounter calendars.** Consecrate is its required connected gameplay consumer; TAC-02, TAC-08 and CHR-05 supply affected operations.

This is a **planning recommendation**, not an accepted implementation contract or authorization to start runtime work.

The accepted sequence reached geometry113 → Ferry114 → Consecration115. The current map deliberately selects no successor. Therefore this recommendation extends that sequence under the owner’s new planning authorization; it must not be described as an already approved next step.

**1. Dependency rationale and accepted prerequisites**

The formal graph remains unchanged:

| Workstream | Existing direct prerequisites |
|---|---|
| TAC-01, the proposed primary workstream | FND-01, FND-02 |
| TAC-02, affected Action integration | TAC-01, RUL-05 |
| TAC-08, affected casting integration | TAC-02, TAC-05, TAC-07 |
| CHR-05, affected class-technique integration | CHR-03, TAC-02, TAC-05, TAC-08 |

The following accepted slices are **scoped operational prerequisites and reusable evidence**, not new graph edges or whole-workstream closures:

| Accepted slice | Exact retained acceptance reference |
|---|---|
| Ordinary Cleric casting, activity and End accounting | [TAC-08 final review](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-15-tac08-cleric-casting/GPT_FINAL_REVIEW.md), response `4380847f-3bdc-5003-b5a1-1803a4fed501` |
| Genuine Cleric resource funding through Long Rest | [MGT-03 final review](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-15-mgt03-cleric-long-rest/GPT_FINAL_REVIEW.md), response `0361603a-8572-5112-896a-d04663473407` |
| Post-recovery encounter, allowance carry and owned epochs | [EXP-07 final review](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-16-exp07-post-recovery/GPT_FINAL_REVIEW.md), response `7ed650ba-0d52-5376-9188-7ee179d7d397` |
| Earned Cleric 3/Bishop, Invocation and Aura | [Bishop final review](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-16-chr03-bishop-runtime/GPT_FINAL_REVIEW.json), response `07ffc865-b1db-5bb0-9204-3e883bc9c559` |
| Declared geometry113 | [TAC-03 final review](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-16-tac03-declared-geometry-runtime/GPT_FINAL_REVIEW.json), response `9e7360a4-f81d-5f06-8884-49e8ef8eda0a` |
| Ferry114 and its transitions | [TAC-10 final acceptance](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-16-tac10-ferry-wraith-runtime/FINAL_ACCEPTANCE.md), response `bc9b7b5d-cbca-5e57-b297-c6fd18cb39db` |
| Consecration115 | [Final acceptance](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-17-chr05-consecration/FINAL_ACCEPTANCE.json), response `a34a0fba-bc6a-51c7-96d3-3a142e4028a7` |

This selection addresses an explicitly mandatory shared integration gap using already owned abilities and established gameplay. It does not require another creature, grant or advancement merely to create a witness.

**Saint/resurrection should remain held.** The [accepted resurrection prerequisite review](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-15-tac06-resurrection/GPT_CONTRACT_REVIEW.md), response `50395a8a-f1f7-58ac-81b6-a9e116e35f09`, did not approve the entire chain. Cleric 3/Bishop does not supply Cleric 16/Saint ownership, the intervening acquisition consequences, genuine death-occurrence/body/soul authority or return-to-schedule integration. These remain separate obligations. Conversely, this calendar module is not a newly invented formal prerequisite for every future advancement.

**2. Concrete behavior and owning APIs**

The required new behavior is: **an otherwise lawful magical Action can execute outside initiative after the actor’s short virtual slot has ended, while its actual ordinary Action allowance remains available, without contradicting activity or Dissonance history.**

The existing three-seat example makes the gap concrete: the owner slot ends at `s+2`, while its ordinary allowance lasts until `s+6`. A new-profile witness at `s+3` must work when all other requirements hold. Merely removing `ConsecrateOpenOwnerSlotRequired` would not satisfy the module.

Use the pinned sources:

- `DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md`: Action limits, outside-combat costs, recharge, Dissonance and Grounding.
- `DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md`: regular markers, event ordering and retained duration endpoints.
- `DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/data/public/class_playtests/cleric.json`: actual technique costs, activity, recharge and protected vent.
- [Shared-world decisions](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/SHARED_WORLD_RULE_DECISIONS.md), TAC-08’s `APPROVED_CASTING_CONTRACT.md` P3/P4, and [Consecration’s corrected contract](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/e7378d055f8bb354312e48de8fb0d70314f4d05d/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-17-chr05-consecration/SOURCE_API_CONTRACT.md) §2.

Bind the original ReviewBible revision `46a4d52728ee6956f0bebcb5d2103ffd5bc67ba4` and each controlling later amendment separately.

The implementation contract should require:

- One shared, versioned activity-context assessment derived from actual actor, epoch, allowance and clock state. Clients cannot supply an interval, completed End, paid flag or activity classification.
- An explicit consumer matrix for `UseConsecrate`, `UseHealingRite`, `UseDivineInvocation`, `CastKnownSpell`, `FocusDetectedAura` and `GroundCastingStrain`. Identify each changed admission rule and preserve source-specific restrictions.
- Existing `ConnectedExpeditionSession.Submit`, `QueryCastingCommand`, `DiscoverCastingCommands`, filtered observations, console dispatch, `Save`, `Restore` and `RecoverBackup` must agree. No independent “activity payment” endpoint.
- Shared Action/RP/Conviction, condition permissions, concentration, exact positions, physical components, inventory custody and work exclusions remain authoritative.
- Consecrate retains Action/2RP, no RNG or clock advance, original zone expiry and separate recharge. Other operations retain their actual dice, costs and effects.
- Calendar transitions preserve spending, original deadlines, recharge and activity provenance. Shared work earns only actual compatible elapsed time.

The principal inspected seams are `SharedSpellCasting.cs`, `SharedConsecration.cs`, `SharedResonance.cs`, `SharedDivineInvocation.cs`, `SpellCastingValidation.cs`, `WorldScheduleRecord.cs`, `LaterEncounterRecords.cs`, and the existing snapshot/query/verified-restoration paths.

**3. Decisions that must close before implementation**

**The calendar amendment is a real prerequisite contract decision.** Existing shared-world policy explicitly ends a slot at the next actor’s Start. TAC-08 settles idle/Grounding decay at that End. The new contract must specify exactly how outside-initiative activity remains admissible without retrospectively changing that settlement.

I recommend investigating a **versioned actor-interval accounting design derived from the existing shared calendar**. This recommendation does not approve moving regular Ends or introducing a second clock.

Before acceptance, the written contract must settle:

- The outside activity interval’s identity, opening, closing and relation to Action refresh.
- Exact idle/Grounding settlement, including zero Dissonance where no End row was previously emitted.
- Entry, closure and carried-allowance behavior, including transitions before the next owner Start.
- Ordering against condition/life events, effect expiry, recharge, work completion and pending choices.
- Which existing magical operations gain the new context and why.

**Stop if the proposed solution requires erasing a settled End, undoing decay, assigning an action to a fictitious future turn, granting an extra allowance, or silently changing historical profiles.** Resolve that design before coding.

Use a fresh opt-in successor profile with its identifier checked for availability. Preserve authentic profiles through115. Pre-reinforcement/bootstrap casting, general roster changes, new abilities, Saint advancement, resurrection, production promotion and Unity remain outside this module and explicitly open where mandatory.

**4. Proposed testable acceptance criteria**

1. **Genuine connected witness:** fresh successor genesis follows lawful exploration, encounters, acquisition, management and funding. After actual encounter closure, execute Consecrate after the old owner-slot End but before the next owner Start, using real remaining Action/RP. Continue through meaningful terrain use, a lawful transition and paid ordinary play. No edited115 save or fabricated history.

2. **Activity correctness:** demonstrate genuine nonzero Dissonance with late magical activity preventing inappropriate idle/Grounding benefit; also qualify idle, Grounding, zero-Dissonance and each changed activity classification. Shared-handler reuse requires validated semantic equivalence.

3. **Timing boundaries:** before/at/after the former slot End; immediately before/at the next owner Start; spent Action; recharge readiness; zone expiry; original deadlines across entry/closure. Whole-interval versus partitioned advancement must yield identical ordered results.

4. **Shared-state interactions:** busy work, traversal, incapacity, concentration, components and pending decisions retain their actual restrictions. Compatible background work progresses exactly once. No new RNG draw, resource recovery, stock duplication or timer reset arises from context selection.

5. **Authority and privacy:** authorized queries/discovery agree with execution and remain pure. Wrong/revoked seats, stale revisions, conflicting payloads, invalid targets and capacity exhaustion preserve canonical state/RNG. Persisted authorized retry is distinct from direct repeat rejection.

6. **Persistence:** save while an outside activity interval is open, after late activation, before/after settlement, and across a real epoch transition. Require strict causal forgery rejection, backup recovery and ordinary continuation. Retain the supported historical matrix and add authentic115 compatibility without backfilling new semantics.

7. **Execution evidence:** complete console uninterrupted/restored, typed uninterrupted/restored and receipt-replay paths; compare named canonical/RNG, filtered-view and ordered-discovery checkpoints. Preserve the1,587 predecessor case inventory and add meaningful new cases. Regression against a new runtime freeze does not restart or replace previously accepted qualification records.

8. **Build and final review:** exact source/policy pins, compiler/options/input/DLL identities, C#9 warnings-as-errors, package checks, actual terminal results, retained failures/corrections and an actual final GPT review with Codex concurrence. No module acceptance from an index alone.

The existing TAC-10 and Consecration cure allocations remain closed within their accepted scope. This module introduces no requirement to retry those searches. Broader performance, UR and whole-engine qualification remain open.

**5. Planning disposition**

Prepare this **single proposed module contract** and its map entry for actual planning review. Retain all49 rows,120 edges and100 completion obligations. Mark the successor as proposed/awaiting contract acceptance, and preserve implementation as paused. No separately implemented prerequisite module is established by this consultation; the unresolved calendar contract must close first.

My review was read-only. I inspected the current status, governing completion criteria, relevant operational sequence, retained reviews, pinned source clauses and selected current API implementations. I independently compared the49 current rows against the historical graph: all120 dependencies and original acceptance texts match. **I did not edit files, execute gameplay/tests/builds/benchmarks, re-audit qualification archives or push anything.**

codexDisposition: Concur with selecting one TAC-01 ordinary-world magical-activity calendar successor for planning review. The actual calendar amendment remains open; this recommendation is not implementation-contract acceptance or runtime authorization.
